newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses gain ground, dollar mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses gain ground, dollar mixed.

text.p: European bourses, nervous over the outlook for Wall Street, the world's biggest stock market, advanced in early trading on Wednesday after a rebound in New York and reassuring news on U.S. interest rates.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar slipped against the yen but rose versus the mark as Japanese trade figures and German money supply data moved it in different directions.
Shares ended higher in New York on Tuesday, recovering from early losses after the Federal Reserve, as generally expected, kept interest rates unchanged.

The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 39.98 points at 6,308.33, erasing the previous day's losses. But U.S. bond prices fell on surprisingly strong November U.S. housing starts, which prompted some nervousness on interest rates further ahead.

London share traders said trading was likely to be thin ahead of Christmas holidays. Investors continued to fret about the risk of a more pronounced drop on Wall Street, which still shows a 26 percent advance this year, even after recent weakness, they added.
"We're in the silly season (pre-Christmas) now and most people are content to stay away until they adjust portfolios in the New Year," one London dealer said.
Adding to question marks over Wall Street's prospects, top stategists at Merrill Lynch said investors might be better off with bonds instead of stocks next year.

But the London stock market, Europe's busiest, took its cue from Wall Street's latest performance to open higher and was also boosted by news of an agreed 1.267 billion pound ($2.11 billion) bid by U.S. group Entergy for London Electricity.
"Bid speculation has been going around the market over the last few days in various sectors. Today's bid will only add fuel to the fire," one trader said.
French shares were aided by the Dow's gains and buoyed by prospects for lower interest rates.
Wall Street's revival helped German shares make a firm start, too, as did a firmer dollar, good news for exporters. Weaker-than-expected German money supply data also helped.
The Bundesbank said growth in its main monetary policy indicator, M3 money supply, slowed to an annualised rate of 8.0 percent in November from 8.4 percent in October.
Economists had expected a more moderate slowdown but said it did not change their view that the central bank was unlikely to amend its policy just now.
The currency market, however, lived in hope of lower German rates and boosted the dollar against the mark as a result.
"The M3 data was just soft enough to keep interest in Thursday's meeting alive," said one trader at a British bank.
The Bundesbank central council meets for the last time this year on Thursday and is set to announce its 1997 M3 growth targets at a news conference afterwards.

Analysts said there was a faint chance the bank might shave its 3.0 percent securities repurchase rate. Market speculation on such a move grew after the Bank of France trimmed its key money rate to 3.15 percent from 3.20 on Tuesday.
On Wednesday, French call money eased to 3-3/16 5/16 from 3-1/4 3/8, giving hope of more rate reductions, analysts said.
The pound, meanwhile, rallied after strong British jobless and retail sales data. British November unemployment fell 95,800 to 1.93 million -- much more than a forecast 26,000 decline.
This should increase the pressure for a rise in interest rates in Britain, dealers said. Sterling rose to $1.6737 and 2.5973 marks from 1.6713 and 2.5845 overnight.
Currency trading was, however, thin ahead of the holiday season. "The Japanese trade data is the main story but the market is struggling to find an interest," said Adrian Schmidt at Chase Manhattan.
The yen stengthened after news of an unexpected 0.2 percent year-on-year rise in Japan's custom-cleared trade surplus and a sharp 31.2 percent rise in its surplus with the United States.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5518 marks and 113.53 yen, compared with 1.5454 and 113.73 in late business on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 21.3 points at 4,000.9.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX was 8.96 higher at 2,824.09.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 15.39 at 2,209.09.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $369 in the morning, compared with the previous London close of $368.95. Silver was steady at $4.87. ($1=.6003 Pound)
